tiles.compose:
# The DIGEST is the pin — a tag stays mutable at the registry however specific it
# looks, so the tag here is human-readable sugar (ADR-0006 Decision 8). Version is
# provisional until the tile clears the hardware bench.
services:
  # Home Assistant refuses a proxied request outright — 400 Bad Request, empty body —
  # when it sees an X-Forwarded-For header it was not told to expect. The node-local
  # Caddy always sets that header, so out of the box every LAN request to this tile
  # failed (bench, 2026-08-23). This one-shot seeds the trust settings BEFORE Home
  # Assistant starts, and exits.
  #
  # WHY THE SETTINGS GO IN .storage/http AND NOT configuration.yaml
  #
  # Since 2026.8 the HTTP settings live in the store at /config/.storage/http, and
  # `http:` in configuration.yaml is a deprecated one-shot import (it breaks in
  # 2027.2.0). The store holds TWO slots, `stable` and `pending`. An imported YAML
  # `http:` block lands in `pending`, and a pending config is a TRIAL: unless an
  # admin promotes it within five minutes, Home Assistant logs
  #
  #   Pending HTTP config was not confirmed within 0:05:00; reverting to the
  #   stable config and restarting
  #
  # marks it `not_promoted`, never applies it again, and restarts on `stable` —
  # which has no proxy trust in it. Promotion is a websocket call behind
  # @require_admin, and on a fresh install NO ACCOUNT EXISTS YET, so there is
  # nobody who can confirm it. That is why seeding configuration.yaml alone made
  # this tile work for exactly five minutes and then permanently un-work itself
  # (bench, 2026-08-29).
  #
  # So the seed writes the settings straight into the `stable` slot with no
  # `pending` alongside. Nothing to confirm, nothing to revert, no restart. It is
  # the same file Home Assistant itself writes on every install, in the schema
  # version this pinned image defines (2.2, read off a running instance) — and if
  # a future image ever moves that schema, Home Assistant's own store migration
  # handles it, and its documented failure path is "discard and fall back to
  # defaults", i.e. back to the 400 this tile started at rather than anything
  # worse. The image is digest-pinned, so that only ever arrives with a
  # deliberate bump.
  #
  # `yaml_migration_done: true` tells Home Assistant the store is already the
  # source of truth, so it never stages a YAML import. Correspondingly there is
  # no `http:` block in the seeded configuration.yaml: with the migration marked
  # done, one present there would only raise a "your YAML is being ignored"
  # repair notice.
  #
  # Both files are seeded only if absent, so a reinstall or an upgrade never
  # clobbers an owner's edits — and an owner who wants to change these settings
  # has Settings > System > Network in the UI, which promotes its own pending
  # config properly.
  #
  # It runs the same pinned Home Assistant image rather than a shell image on purpose:
  # nothing new to pull, nothing new to arch-probe, nothing new to vouch for.
  home-assistant-config-seed:
    image: ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:2026.10.4@sha256:23f4dfbb69ce76315dbc4de7915504f1c2dcecd7ca2648113a493a385972e133
    restart: "no"
    entrypoint:
      - /bin/sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -eu
        mkdir -p /config/.storage

        if [ -f /config/configuration.yaml ]; then
          echo "configuration.yaml already present - leaving it alone"
        else
          cat > /config/configuration.yaml <<'YAML'
        # Seeded by Rasputin when this app was installed.
        #
        # Home Assistant is reached through the node-local reverse proxy, which
        # forwards your real client address in X-Forwarded-For. Home Assistant has
        # to be told to trust that proxy or it answers every request with
        # 400 Bad Request.
        #
        # Those trust settings are NOT in this file. Since 2026.8 they live in the
        # store, and Rasputin seeded them there when it installed this app. Change
        # them in the UI under Settings > System > Network, not here — an `http:`
        # block added to this file is now ignored.

        default_config:

        automation: !include automations.yaml
        script: !include scripts.yaml
        scene: !include scenes.yaml
        YAML
          printf '%s\n' '[]' > /config/automations.yaml
          printf '%s\n' '{}' > /config/scripts.yaml
          printf '%s\n' '[]' > /config/scenes.yaml
          echo "seeded /config/configuration.yaml"
        fi

        if [ -f /config/.storage/http ]; then
          echo ".storage/http already present - leaving it alone"
        else
          # $$ is a literal $ — compose interpolates the compose file before the
          # shell ever sees this script.
          now="$$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S+00:00')"
          cat > /config/.storage/http <<JSON
        {
          "version": 2,
          "minor_version": 2,
          "key": "http",
          "data": {
            "stable": {
              "server_port": 8123,
              "use_x_forwarded_for": true,
              "trusted_proxies": [
                "127.0.0.1/32",
                "::1/128"
              ],
              "login_attempts_threshold": -1,
              "ip_ban_enabled": true,
              "cors_allowed_origins": [
                "https://cast.home-assistant.io"
              ],
              "ssl_profile": "modern",
              "use_x_frame_options": true,
              "created_at": "$$now",
              "error": null,
              "error_message": null
            },
            "pending": null,
            "yaml_migration_done": true
          }
        }
        JSON
          chmod 600 /config/.storage/http
          echo "seeded /config/.storage/http"
        fi
    volumes:
      - homeassistant-config:/config

  home-assistant:
    image: ghcr.io/home-assistant/home-assistant:2026.10.4@sha256:23f4dfbb69ce76315dbc4de7915504f1c2dcecd7ca2648113a493a385972e133
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      home-assistant-config-seed:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    # Host networking is what makes local discovery work — mDNS, SSDP, DHCP
    # sniffing and matter/thread all need the LAN broadcast domain directly.
    # In bridge mode Home Assistant runs but finds almost nothing, which is
    # the feature people install it for. Declared, not silent.
    network_mode: host
    environment:
      TZ: UTC
    volumes:
      - homeassistant-config:/config

volumes:
  homeassistant-config:

tiles.compose:
# Rasputin app-catalog tile — the compose half.
#
# THIS FILE IS NOT RUN BY `docker compose` FROM THIS REPO IN NORMAL USE. It is
# the stack a Rasputin control plane deploys. The standalone stack is
# deploy/docker-compose.yml. deploy/test-tile-secrets.sh does run THIS file, on a
# throwaway project, to prove the secret handling below end to end.
#
#   * `ghcr.io/geekdojo/human-system@sha256:66620962dce4e19d8d73b7326ac82aa6a30f80fdc27536ccdd7fb7061307d18e` is substituted by .github/workflows/release.yml with the
#     digest of the image that release actually pushed. A catalog tile MUST be
#     digest-pinned: tileschema.validateImagePin refuses a tag reference however
#     specific the tag looks, because a tag stays mutable at the registry.
#
# On adoption this file is copied into a catalog repo as
# `tiles/human-system/docker-compose.yml`, beside `tile.json`. See geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md.
#
# The tile is `status: available` (2026-09-10), so a control plane installs this
# stack, and tools/tilecheck validates the manifest together with it. The §4.4
# restore round-trip of hs-db (into the same app, opened with the key the
# platform holds) is still owed before it should ship to anyone:
# geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md §B4.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ONE CONTAINER. The Postgres sidecar is gone (SQLite port, milestone 3): the
# database is a FILE the app opens in process through a pure-Go driver. The
# one-shot that used to generate this app's secret is gone too (geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#606).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE SECRET IS THE PLATFORM'S. This stack generates nothing and holds nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# There is ONE secret, `app-secret-key`, and it reaches the app as HS_SECRET_KEY
# in its environment. It encrypts the stored Anthropic API key, keys the CSRF
# HMAC, and -- since 2026-09-22 -- UNWRAPS THE DATA KEY THE DATABASE ITSELF IS
# ENCRYPTED UNDER. Change it or lose it and human-system.db on hs-db is
# unreadable, permanently, by anyone.
#
# The control plane makes it (ADR-0006 Decision 11a, the `tile.secrets`
# capability deploy/tile.json declares). On this app's first deploy it derives a
# 32-byte value from the cluster seed, bound to this app's id and the secret's
# name, and stores it as `apps/<appID>/app-secret-key`; from then on the stored
# entry is the value. So it is the same across a redeploy, a node move, an
# upgrade and a restore into the same app, and no operator can read it back.
# Deleting the app destroys it, so the app's own export is the owner's copy of
# the record outside the platform.
# geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md §B5 and SPEC §12.5.
#
# The token below is replaced at deploy by an environment reference, and the
# value is handed to `docker compose` in its environment rather than written
# to a file the stack mounts. This comment never spells the token, because the
# catalog check reads comments too.
#
# A missing value (a control plane that substituted nothing) stops the app with
# "HS_SECRET_KEY (or HS_SECRET_KEY_FILE): required environment variable is not
# set" before it opens any database; a value that is not base64 of 32 bytes
# stops it with "HS_SECRET_KEY: environment variable is invalid";
# a valid value that is not this database's key refuses with the wrong-key error
# and leaves the database untouched. deploy/test-tile-secrets.sh proves all
# three on this file.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

services:
  app:
    image: ghcr.io/geekdojo/human-system@sha256:66620962dce4e19d8d73b7326ac82aa6a30f80fdc27536ccdd7fb7061307d18e
    restart: unless-stopped

    environment:
      # The SQLite database FILE inside the hs-db volume mounted below. No host,
      # no user, no password, and so no DSN to keep a credential out of. The
      # file is created on first start; the DIRECTORY is not, so a volume that
      # failed to mount is a loud start-up error rather than a new empty
      # database written into the container's own filesystem.
      #
      # THE FILE IS ENCRYPTED, and so are the -wal and -shm beside it. The key
      # sidecar `human-system.db.profile.json` sits beside them in the same
      # volume: it holds a copy of the data key wrapped under HS_SECRET_KEY, and
      # it is useless without that secret. See the hs-db volume note below.
      HS_DATABASE_PATH: "/db/human-system.db"
      # The platform's derived, store-held secret. See the header.
      HS_SECRET_KEY: "${secret:app-secret-key}"
      # MCP write tools stay off in the tile: this is left unset and the
      # operator supplies a token when they want agent writes (SPEC §12.8).
      HS_MCP_TOKEN: ""
      # THE ORIGIN IS OWNED BY THE APP, not supplied at install (2026-09-10).
      #
      # There is deliberately no HS_ORIGIN here. Its only consumer is WebAuthn
      # (passkeys); CSRF never reads it. The node's Caddy reaches this app at
      # one or both of these names, and passes the name through as `Host`:
      #
      #   https://human-system.<cluster-id>.internal       always (tailnet)
      #   https://human-system.lan.<cluster-id>.internal   when LAN exposure is on
      #
      # <cluster-id> is the cluster's id, or `rasputin` on an unnamed cluster.
      # HS_ORIGIN_FROM_PROXY tells the app to read its origin from that Host,
      # accept ONLY those two shapes, and treat each as its own passkey relying
      # party: the RP ID is the name the request arrived on, so a passkey made
      # on one name works on that name only (SPEC §12.6). It is
      # safe here, and only here, because of the loopback binding in `ports:`
      # below: nothing but the node's own Caddy can send this app a Host. An
      # explicit HS_ORIGIN, if one is ever added, wins. geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md §B2.
      HS_ORIGIN_FROM_PROXY: "true"
      HS_LISTEN: ":8080"
      # Every route into this tile is https, terminated by the node's Caddy, so
      # the session cookie is marked Secure. (The leg from Caddy to this
      # container is plain http on loopback; the browser never sees it.)
      HS_SECURE_COOKIES: "true"
      # No HS_CATALOG_TOKEN, deliberately: the tile has no way to be handed
      # one, and a public catalog does not need one. The app fetches the
      # release anonymously; the catalog repository is public. Were it ever
      # private again, that fetch would be refused and Settings would say so
      # ("not reachable without a token; the repository may be private").
      # geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md §B6.
      HS_CATALOG_REPO: "geekdojo/human-system-substance-catalog"
      HS_DATA_DIR: "/data"
      HS_SEED_DEMO: "false"

    # LOOPBACK ONLY. The node's Caddy dials 127.0.0.1:8085, so the proxy is
    # unaffected. Published on every interface, anyone on the LAN could reach
    # the app at <node-ip>:8085, skip the proxy, and send any Host they like —
    # and HS_ORIGIN_FROM_PROXY above reads the origin from that Host. Bound to
    # 127.0.0.1, only this node can connect. (Rasputin enforcing loopback for
    # every tile is tracked as geekdojo/geekdojo-brain#404.)
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8085:8080"

    volumes:
      # Named volumes, not bind mounts: named volumes are rooted on the node's
      # `persistent` partition and survive a RAUC A/B OS update by construction.
      #
      # hs-db is now mounted on the APP, read-write, because the app IS the
      # database engine. It holds human-system.db, the -wal and -shm files SQLite
      # keeps beside it, and human-system.db.profile.json, the key sidecar; all
      # four must sit on the same filesystem, which is why the mount is a
      # directory and HS_DATABASE_PATH names a file inside it rather than the
      # volume being mounted as the file itself. The sidecar in particular MUST
      # be on the same filesystem: it is published by rename, which is atomic
      # only within one.
      - hs-db:/db
      - hs-data:/data

    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "/usr/local/bin/healthcheck", "-url", "http://127.0.0.1:8080/healthz"]
      interval: 15s
      timeout: 3s
      start_period: 20s
      retries: 5

    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true

volumes:
  hs-data:
  # The SQLite database file (ENCRYPTED), its -wal and its -shm (also encrypted),
  # and the plaintext key sidecar.
  #
  # A COPY OF THIS VOLUME IS NOISE WITHOUT THIS APP'S SECRET. The database is
  # encrypted under a data key that is written down nowhere; what IS written down
  # is a copy of it wrapped under HS_SECRET_KEY, which the platform holds for this
  # app id. A restore into the same app gets it back from the platform with no
  # action; a copy restored anywhere else opens nothing.
  # geekdojo-brain: projects/human-system/reference/deploy.md B4.
  #
  # Declared in deploy/tile.json
  # as `backup: critical` / `quiesce: stop`, and BOTH are still exactly right —
  # but `quiesce: stop` is right for a NEW reason, and an operator reading a
  # backup policy deserves the real one.
  #
  # With Postgres, stopping was about not copying a running server's data
  # directory: a live postmaster mutates files under the copy and a backup taken
  # that way restores as a corrupt cluster.
  #
  # With SQLite it is about the write-ahead log. A transaction can COMMIT and
  # live entirely in `human-system.db-wal` until a checkpoint folds it into
  # `human-system.db`. A backup that copies the main file while the app is
  # running — or that copies all three at three different instants — can
  # therefore be missing writes that were committed and acknowledged, and it
  # will restore silently, looking like a database that is simply a little
  # behind. Stopping the app first is what closes that window: Store.Close runs
  # `PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)`, so a cleanly stopped install leaves every
  # committed byte in the main file and a ZERO-LENGTH -wal. Clean shutdown is
  # load-bearing for backup correctness in a way it simply was not before.
  hs-db:

tiles.compose:
# The DIGEST is the pin — a tag stays mutable at the registry however specific it
# looks, so the tag here is human-readable sugar (ADR-0006 Decision 8). Version is
# provisional until the tile clears the hardware bench.
services:
  immich-server:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-server:v3.3.5@sha256:485d546a2e31d6a8b4db8423fcba5c109de8c218d93410af115fd1ccfc4352a6
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      redis:
        condition: service_started
      database:
        condition: service_started
      # immich-server starts only once the bridge below has put the database
      # on the platform's password.
      immich-db-bridge:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DB_HOSTNAME: database
      DB_USERNAME: immich
      DB_DATABASE_NAME: immich
      # Internal to this stack's network — postgres publishes no port.
      DB_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-password}"
      REDIS_HOSTNAME: redis
    volumes:
      - immich-upload:/data
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:2283:2283"

  immich-machine-learning:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/immich-machine-learning:v3.3.5@sha256:5b28c9352c8374b8a1ed96fbdd8d6755fea6e43510ec43fdf6538aa02ea40f56
    restart: unless-stopped
    volumes:
      - immich-model-cache:/cache

  redis:
    image: valkey/valkey:9@sha256:3add1a336a920ea54770a001ab6feb3da5fceea96a40373a3a2cd469b815f0b7
    restart: unless-stopped

  database:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0@sha256:bcf63357191b76a916ae5eb93464d65c07511da41e3bf7a8416db519b40b1c23
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: immich
      # Postgres applies this only when it first creates its data directory.
      # An install from before this tile used the platform's secrets still has
      # the old published password; immich-db-bridge moves it.
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-password}"
      POSTGRES_DB: immich
      POSTGRES_INITDB_ARGS: "--data-checksums"
    volumes:
      - immich-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data

  # One-shot, on every deploy, restart and restore (`restart: "no"`, and
  # immich-server waits for it to exit 0). It moves a database still on the
  # password this tile used to publish onto the platform's:
  #   1. Wait for the database to answer, at most 120 seconds. The agent's
  #      default deploy budget for this tile is 300 seconds, so a database that
  #      never answers fails the deploy with this bridge's own sentence first.
  #   2. If the immich role logs in with the platform's password, do nothing.
  #   3. Otherwise log in as immich (the database's superuser) with the
  #      published legacy password and change it to the platform's.
  #   4. Fail, and so keep immich-server stopped, when neither password is
  #      accepted or anything else goes wrong. Each failure prints its own
  #      sentence.
  # Passwords reach psql only through PGPASSWORD, and the new one reaches the
  # server on stdin from the shell's printf builtin: never a command line.
  #
  # LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD is the password this tile published before it used the
  # platform's secrets. It is public, and grants nothing once a database has
  # been moved. Shipping it is the recorded R4 exception in EXCEPTIONS.md.
  #
  # Reverting the app to its previous version after this upgrade leaves
  # immich-server unable to log in to its database: the database keeps the
  # platform's password and the previous version has no bridge. The recovery
  # is to upgrade again; the bridge then finds the platform's password in place.
  immich-db-bridge:
    image: ghcr.io/immich-app/postgres:14-vectorchord0.4.3-pgvectors0.2.0@sha256:bcf63357191b76a916ae5eb93464d65c07511da41e3bf7a8416db519b40b1c23
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      - database
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-password}"
      LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD: immich
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -u
        deadline=$$(( $$(date +%s) + 120 ))
        until pg_isready -q -h database -t 5; do
          if [ "$$(date +%s)" -ge "$$deadline" ]; then
            echo "The database did not answer within 120 seconds, so immich will not start."
            exit 1
          fi
          sleep 1
        done
        # login PASSWORD: 0 logged in, 1 password refused (28P01), 2 any other
        # failure.
        login() {
          err=$$(PGPASSWORD="$$1" psql -w -X -q -h database -U immich -d immich -c 'SELECT 1' 2>&1 >/dev/null) && return 0
          case "$$err" in *"password authentication failed"*|*28P01*) return 1 ;; esac
          return 2
        }
        other() {
          echo "Could not log in to the database for a reason other than a refused password, so immich will not start."
          exit 1
        }
        login "$$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"
        case $$? in
          0) echo "The database already uses the platform's password."; exit 0 ;;
          2) other ;;
        esac
        login "$$LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD"
        case $$? in
          1) echo "The database refused both the platform's and the published legacy password, so immich will not start."; exit 1 ;;
          2) other ;;
        esac
        if ! printf "ALTER ROLE immich PASSWORD '%s';\n" "$$POSTGRES_PASSWORD" | PGPASSWORD="$$LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD" psql -w -X -q -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -h database -U immich -d immich >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Logged in to the database but could not change its password, so immich will not start."
          exit 1
        fi
        if ! login "$$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"; then
          echo "Changed the database's password, but the immich role still refuses the platform's password, so immich will not start."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "Moved the database from the published legacy password to the platform's."

volumes:
  immich-upload:
  immich-model-cache:
  immich-db:

tiles.compose:
# The DIGEST is the pin — a tag stays mutable at the registry however specific it
# looks, so the tag here is human-readable sugar (ADR-0006 Decision 8). Version is
# provisional until the tile clears the hardware bench.
services:
  romm:
    image: rommapp/romm:5.4.1@sha256:8677fb7b81b1d3db20b849e989a1dadc2a11159e51eb34a2acdcb01102274edf
    restart: unless-stopped
    depends_on:
      romm-db:
        condition: service_started
      # romm starts only once the bridge below has put the database on the
      # platform's passwords.
      romm-db-bridge:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    environment:
      DB_HOST: romm-db
      DB_NAME: romm
      DB_USER: romm
      # Internal to this stack's network — mariadb publishes no port.
      DB_PASSWD: "${secret:db-password}"
      ROMM_AUTH_SECRET_KEY: "${secret:auth-secret-key}"
    volumes:
      - romm-resources:/romm/resources
      - romm-config:/romm/config
      - romm-library:/romm/library
      - romm-assets:/romm/assets
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:8084:8080"

  romm-db:
    image: mariadb:12.3.3@sha256:d46e102fa8b9b72bfcdeb56f9dd538742092119dc8b11f31fe662605cd234cd9
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      MARIADB_DATABASE: romm
      MARIADB_USER: romm
      # MariaDB applies these two only when it first creates its data
      # directory. An install from before this tile used the platform's
      # secrets still has the old published passwords; romm-db-bridge moves it.
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-password}"
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-root-password}"
    volumes:
      - romm-db:/var/lib/mysql

  # One-shot, on every deploy, restart and restore (`restart: "no"`, and romm
  # waits for it to exit 0). It moves a database still on the passwords this
  # tile used to publish onto the platform's:
  #   1. Wait for romm-db to answer, at most 120 seconds. The agent's default
  #      deploy budget for this tile is 300 seconds, so a database that never
  #      answers fails the deploy with this bridge's own sentence first.
  #   2. If the romm account logs in with the platform's password, do nothing.
  #   3. Otherwise log in as root with the platform's root password, then with
  #      the published legacy one, and change root and romm to the platform's
  #      passwords. romm's account is changed last, so step 2 passing means
  #      every account was changed.
  #   4. Fail, and so keep romm stopped, when neither root password is accepted
  #      or anything else goes wrong. Each failure prints its own sentence.
  # Passwords reach the client only through MYSQL_PWD, and the new ones reach
  # the server on stdin from the shell's printf builtin: never a command line.
  #
  # LEGACY_* are the passwords this tile published before it used the
  # platform's secrets. They are public, and grant nothing once a database has
  # been moved. Shipping them is the recorded R4 exception in EXCEPTIONS.md.
  #
  # Reverting the app to its previous version after this upgrade leaves romm
  # unable to log in to its database: the database keeps the platform's
  # passwords and the previous version has no bridge. The recovery is to
  # upgrade again; the bridge then finds the platform's passwords in place.
  romm-db-bridge:
    image: mariadb:12.3.3@sha256:d46e102fa8b9b72bfcdeb56f9dd538742092119dc8b11f31fe662605cd234cd9
    restart: "no"
    depends_on:
      - romm-db
    environment:
      MARIADB_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-password}"
      MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD: "${secret:db-root-password}"
      LEGACY_DB_PASSWORD: romm
      LEGACY_ROOT_PASSWORD: romm-root
    command:
      - sh
      - -c
      - |
        set -u
        deadline=$$(( $$(date +%s) + 120 ))
        until mariadb-admin --protocol=tcp -h romm-db --connect-timeout=5 ping >/dev/null 2>&1; do
          if [ "$$(date +%s)" -ge "$$deadline" ]; then
            echo "The database did not answer within 120 seconds, so romm will not start."
            exit 1
          fi
          sleep 1
        done
        # login USER PASSWORD: 0 logged in, 1 password refused (ERROR 1045),
        # 2 any other failure.
        login() {
          err=$$(MYSQL_PWD="$$2" mariadb --protocol=tcp -h romm-db -u "$$1" -e 'SELECT 1' 2>&1 >/dev/null) && return 0
          case "$$err" in *"ERROR 1045"*) return 1 ;; esac
          return 2
        }
        other() {
          echo "Could not log in to the database for a reason other than a refused password, so romm will not start."
          exit 1
        }
        login romm "$$MARIADB_PASSWORD"
        case $$? in
          0) echo "The database already uses the platform's passwords."; exit 0 ;;
          2) other ;;
        esac
        root_password=$$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD
        login root "$$root_password"
        case $$? in
          1)
            root_password=$$LEGACY_ROOT_PASSWORD
            login root "$$root_password"
            case $$? in
              1) echo "The database refused both the platform's and the published legacy root password, so romm will not start."; exit 1 ;;
              2) other ;;
            esac
            ;;
          2) other ;;
        esac
        if ! printf "ALTER USER 'root'@'localhost' IDENTIFIED BY '%s';\nALTER USER 'root'@'%%' IDENTIFIED BY '%s';\nALTER USER 'romm'@'%%' IDENTIFIED BY '%s';\n" "$$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$$MARIADB_ROOT_PASSWORD" "$$MARIADB_PASSWORD" | MYSQL_PWD="$$root_password" mariadb --protocol=tcp -h romm-db -uroot >/dev/null 2>&1; then
          echo "Logged in to the database as root but could not change its passwords, so romm will not start."
          exit 1
        fi
        if ! login romm "$$MARIADB_PASSWORD"; then
          echo "Changed the database's passwords, but the romm account still refuses the platform's password, so romm will not start."
          exit 1
        fi
        echo "Moved the database from the published legacy passwords to the platform's."

volumes:
  romm-resources:
  romm-config:
  romm-library:
  romm-assets:
  romm-db:
